reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource context, full AdverseEvent StructureDefinition report, local R4/R6 StructureDefinitions, deterministic aggregate, and behavior reports for direct AdverseEvent applicability. The aggregate was treated as prior context only. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as base-resource context, not as AdverseEvent-specific evidence.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 AdverseEvent is FMM 0 trial-use, so the compatibility burden is weaker than for mature or normative resources. That lowers the threshold for accepting a broad R6 remodel, but it does not eliminate concern for adverse-event data used in patient safety, pharmacovigilance, regulated clinical research, or audit workflows.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 keeps AdverseEvent but substantially remodels its core content, making a resource-level migration program unavoidable while still leaving several low-cost or safety-sensitive compatibility breaks worth preserving or revisiting.

reasoning.thesisMd: AdverseEvent is not removed, but R6 changes enough central local content that migration cannot be treated as a validator/codegen refresh. Existing R4 instances may need a required lifecycle `status`, field renames, scalar-to-array rewrites, Reference-to-CodeableReference wrapping, classification into new semantic buckets, and expert policy for severity and causality.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a major model remodel with stable resource identity. The hardest forward breaks are the mandatory modifier `status`; `event` to `code`; `date` to `effect[x]`; `resultingCondition` to `resultingEffect`; removal of top-level `severity`; `contributor` to `participant`; `subjectMedicalHistory`/`referenceDocument` split into supporting/contributing/action fields; `suspectEntity.instance` becoming CodeableReference; and `suspectEntity.causality` changing from repeatable backbone to singleton with renamed/removed children. Several of these require clinical or implementation-guide mapping policy, not just syntactic transforms.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a migration program is already unavoidable, preventing every individual wire break is not the highest-leverage strategy. However, that does not make additional break prevention valueless. Low-cost preservation or transition support still matters most where the old element is central, where data loss or expert judgment is likely, or where regulated/safety workflows depend on the data. In this resource, `severity`, repeatable causality details, and the same-purpose `event`/`code` rename remain worth standards attention even though broader remodeling proceeds.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking candidates are retaining `severity` as deprecated/legacy until a clear R6 home is available; keeping `suspectEntity.causality` repeatable or preserving legacy children such as `productRelatedness`; and avoiding a same-type `event` to `code` rename through a deprecated alias or stronger transition mapping. By contrast, making `status` optional would weaken the modifier/lifecycle goal, and retaining parallel legacy fields for every CodeableReference or participant remodel would create substantial duplicate-representation and reconciliation costs.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinitions, SearchParameters, or HTTP REST behavior findings affected AdverseEvent. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant to servers and clients as base FHIR behavior changes, but they do not change the AdverseEvent-specific migration conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is already unavoidable and that the shape is a `major-model-remodel`. I do not fully agree with its `migration-program-dominates` leverage conclusion. The aggregate appears to over-weight the count of hard breaks and under-weight the remaining practical value of low-cost preservation for `severity`, causality, and the avoidable `event`/`code` rename.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for structural migration shape because both R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were available locally. The main uncertainties are terminology expansion details for SNOMED/external value sets and any official HL7 rationale or narrative guidance not present in the computable packages.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds mandatory modifier element AdverseEvent.status
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Every migrated R4 instance needs a new 1..1 modifier status and implementers must decide lifecycle state, so this is a real resource-level migration driver. The break appears proportionate because `entered-in-error` status changes whether the event should be treated as valid clinical information.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.event is renamed to AdverseEvent.code and its example value set changes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a same-purpose optional CodeableConcept rename that breaks JSON and generated APIs with limited apparent safety benefit. Even with FMM 0, a deprecated legacy element, alias-like transition, or explicit compatibility mapping looks comparatively low cost.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.date is replaced by choice element AdverseEvent.effect[x]
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 `date` must become `effectDateTime`, while R6 can represent `effectPeriod`. The rename plus semantic shift from event date toward effect timing contributes to the need for explicit migration policy, though retaining both fields would create precedence ambiguity.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.resultingCondition is replaced by CodeableReference AdverseEvent.resultingEffect
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: A repeating Condition Reference becomes a CodeableReference that can also point to Observation or carry a concept. R4 data needs renaming and wrapping, and reverse conversion of R6 concept-only or Observation effects is lossy.

findingConsiderations.title: Top-level AdverseEvent.severity is removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Severity is clinically and regulated-reporting significant, and R6 has no direct local AdverseEvent replacement. Forcing existing severity into a resulting Condition/Observation or extension is not mechanical, so a deprecated legacy element or official transition path would materially reduce avoidable loss.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.contributor is replaced by participant backbone entries
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Old contributor references can often map to `participant.actor`, but the backbone shape and optional function create API and transform work. The R6 participant model is plausibly justified and preserving a parallel contributor list would create duplicate representation.

findingConsiderations.title: Subject history and reference documents are split into supportingInfo, contributingFactor, and action fields
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is one of the clearest non-mechanical remodels: old history/document references must be wrapped and classified as background support, contributing factor, preventive action, mitigating action, or similar R6 buckets. That classification can require clinical or IG policy.

findingConsiderations.title: suspectEntity.instance changes from Reference to CodeableReference with expanded targets
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The path remains but the JSON/type shape changes from bare Reference to CodeableReference. Existing references need wrapping, and R6's concept-only or expanded-target suspect entities cannot be represented directly in R4.

findingConsiderations.title: suspectEntity.causality is limited to one entry and its children are renamed or removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This remains standards-review-worthy despite the broader remodel. Reducing many causality assessments to one and dropping local `productRelatedness` can lose independent assessments in pharmacovigilance or clinical research workflows. Keeping repetition or legacy children would be more compatibility-preserving than forcing merge/discard policy.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.category binding weakens from extensible to example and the category vocabulary appears to shift
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not a forward hard break because the binding is relaxed from extensible to example. It may affect analytics and terminology guidance, but it does not materially drive the R4-to-R6 instance migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.outcome becomes repeatable and changes from required local codes to example SNOMED binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The binding relaxation is forward-compatible, but the scalar-to-array wire/API change still requires migration for populated R4 instances. This is a local chore once the resource remodel is accepted, and the repeatable outcome model is a reasonable R6 tradeoff.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.actuality required value set adds code unknown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Adding `unknown` creates R6-to-R4 downgrade loss but does not invalidate R4 `actual` or `potential` instances. It does not materially affect forward migration planning.

findingConsiderations.title: AdverseEvent.identifier maximum cardinality increases from 1 to many
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Populated R4 JSON changes from a scalar Identifier to an array, so codegen and transforms must handle it. Still, allowing multiple identifiers is a conventional FHIR expressivity improvement and not a standards-review priority.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional local fields with no direct R4 home
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These optional additions are not forward breaking for R4-to-R6 instances. They only create ordinary R6-to-R4 representability loss if new R6-only data is populated.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context may matter to general R6 client/server migration, but it is not specific to AdverseEvent and should not be counted as a resource-level AdverseEvent behavior break.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Create an explicit AdverseEvent R4-to-R6 migration map covering status assignment, field renames, scalar-to-array changes, Reference-to-CodeableReference wrapping, and the classification of old history/document references into R6 supporting/contributing/action fields.

Revisit or formally justify the `severity` removal and `suspectEntity.causality` singleton/remodel. If the clean R6 model is retained, publish authoritative cross-version guidance for preserving legacy severity, multiple causality assessments, and `productRelatedness`.

Consider a low-cost transition strategy for `event` to `code`, such as a deprecated legacy element, alias-like tooling support, or an official StructureMap/ConceptMap plus generated-client migration guidance.
Before final production transforms, expand and compare the relevant R4/R6 value sets for `event`/`code`, `category`, and `outcome`, including SNOMED and terminology.hl7.org dependencies.

caveats: No direct AdverseEvent behavior/API findings were found in the supplied behavior reports.
Official HL7 change rationale, narrative pages, and cross-version maps were not available in the local inputs reviewed here.
Terminology conclusions involving SNOMED or external terminology.hl7.org value sets should be confirmed with versioned expansion services.
The low R4 maturity weakens stability pressure but does not eliminate safety or regulated-reporting concerns for selected fields.
